full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. These criminal appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgement and order dated 10.12.2006 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15729 of 2005 with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 746 of 2006 making the Rules absolute. 

 2. Criminal Review Petition No. 11 of 2010 arises out of an order of this Division dated 20.07.2008 passed in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 63 of 2007 which had been filed challenging the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 15.06.2006 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15725 of 2005. 

 3. The facts of the case, in short, are that the Security and Exchange Commission, through Md. Mizanur Rahman (present appellant before the Court), Director (Law), Securities and Exchange Commission, on 06.10.2005, filed Complaint Case No. 2909 of 2005 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, against the accused-respondents and others for commission of offence under sections 5(1)(ka), 5(2), 13(2) and 15(1) of the Depository Act, 1999 ("the Act") and punishable under the said Act. On examination of the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure summons were issued against all the accused persons by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. It was narrated in the petition of complaint that in order to procure, through machination, substantial part of the initial shares of Premier Bank Limited valued at taka 55,75,49,700.00 (fifty five crore seventy five lac forty nine thousand and seven hundred takas only), the accused-respondents violated requirement, of sections 5(1)(Ka), 5(2), 13(2) and 15(1) of the Act. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on such statement of the complainant took cognizance of the case and issued summons against the present respondents and 8(eight) others. The accused persons appeared and were enlarged on bail and, thereafter, accused Md. Sayadur Rahman filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15729 of 2005 and accused Saiful Islam filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 746 of 2006 both under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) before the High Court Division and obtained Rules. 

 5. Mr. A.F. Hassan Arif, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that the High Court Division committed serious error of law in grossly misreading and misconstruing the complaint petition holding that the said complaint was not legally entertain-able not having been filed by Security and Exchange Commission, inasmuch as the said complaint was duly lodged by the Commission through its duly authorised human agent which was apparent from the cause title of the complaint and paragraph 1, 5, 7 and 19 of the complaint and the averments disclosed that the complaint had been filed by the Commission through the duly authorised agent. He further submitted that the High Court Division committed gross error of law in holding that unless the account (beneficiary account) was activated, no offence was disclosed which is punishable under the Act, and that since no offence was disclosed the case was instituted wrongly. He submitted that the very opening of Beneficiary Owners (BO) Account without genuine/ real bank account and/or based on fictitious bank account was violation of the requirement of the law, i.e. Depository Act 1999 read with Depositories (Baboharik) Regulation, and for such violation the initiation of the case was in accordance with law. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in misconstruing section 5 and the provision of section 15 of the Depository Act in holding that "we do not find that for breach of any of the sub-section of section 5 penal action can be taken". In this regard he submitted that the requirement of the provisions of section 5 are mandatory and any breach thereof is punishable under section 15 of the Act and that the opening of the BO account on the basis of fictitious bank account is violative of and in breach of provision of the Depository Act and the complaint does disclose an offence. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in misconstruing and misreading subsection (2) of section 5 of the Act in holding "subsection (3) spoke that for any breaches of any of the condition of subsection (1) action might be taken as per Rule", whereas subsection (2) of section 5 of the Act reads as follow: 

 6. And as such the finding of the High Court Division involves interpretation of law of public importance. He further submitted that the judgement and order passed by the High Court Division was erroneous in the light of the facts and circumstances and relevant law of the case in question and as such the appeal may be allowed. He lastly submitted that on the very face of the record and in any view of the matter, the appeal should be allowed as some disputed questions of facts should be decided in the trial, and the High Court Division erred in quashing the proceedings. 

 12. The High Court Division took the view that the proceeding was initiated in the wrong forum and hence could not continue. Support was taken from the earlier decision dated 15.06.2006 of the same Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.15725 of 2005, where the case against other co-accused named in the same Petition Case No. 2905 of 2005 and standing on the same footing had been quashed. The High Court Division took the view that the proceeding having been initiated before a Magistrate, and not before the Court of Sessions it suffers from coram non judice. Against that judgement and order Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.63 of 2007 was filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission, which was dismissed as barred by limitation by judgement and order of this Division dated 20.07.2008. Against that order of this Division the appellant has filed Criminal Review Petition No. 11 of 2010, which is pending and is appearing in the cause list for disposal. 

 15. As noted earlier, the Director (Legal) filed the complaint on behalf of the Commission and, therefore, prima facie it appears that the first part of section 16 has not been contravened. The second part of the section specifies that the Court of Sessions only is empowered to hold trial under this law. The facts disclosed do not indicate that the Magistrate who took cognizance is proceeding with the trial of the case. There appears to be a lacuna in the law, inasmuch as the Act does not provide whether the Court of Sessions will take cognizance or the Code of Criminal Procedure would apply and the Magistrate Court would therefore be competent to take cognizance, and then forward the case to the appropriate Court for trial, which would be the Court of Sessions. 

 21. The facts and circumstances of Criminal Review Petition No. 11 of 2010 being similar, the respondents therein (who are accused in the same Petition Case No. 2905 of 2005) are equally bound to face the trial as the respondents in the instant criminal appeals. Accordingly, the earlier order passed by this Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 63 of 2007 dismissing the same as bared by limitation is hereby recalled. The delay in filing the said criminal petition for leave to appeal is condoned. The judgement and order of the High Court Division dated 15.06.2006 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 15725 of 2005 is set aside. Criminal Review Petition No. 11 of 2010 is accordingly disposed of.
